beats.title: Akhenaten Founds Atenism
beats.description: An Egyptian pharaoh elevated the sun disc above all other gods and built a new capital to worship it alone.
beats.note: Approximate; year 5 of Akhenaten's reign, when Akhetaten was founded.

beats.title: Pentecost and the Church Begins
beats.description: Followers of a crucified Galilean teacher gathered in Jerusalem and began preaching his resurrection, starting a new movement.

beats.title: Mani Begins Manichaeism
beats.description: A Persian prophet announced a revelation from a divine twin and founded a dualist faith that spread from Rome to China.

beats.title: Antony Withdraws to the Desert
beats.description: An Egyptian Christian gave away his wealth and sought solitude in the wilderness, inspiring generations of hermits.

beats.title: Pachomius Founds a Monastery
beats.description: A former soldier in Upper Egypt gathered monks under a common rule, creating communal monastic life.
beats.note: Sources give a window of 318-323; 323 used.

beats.title: Benedict Founds Monte Cassino
beats.description: An Italian abbot built a monastery on a hilltop and wrote a rule that shaped Western monastic life.
beats.why_in: founding of a religious order's house

beats.title: Muhammad's First Revelation
beats.description: A merchant meditating in a cave near Mecca reported a visitation by the angel Gabriel, the start of Islam.

beats.title: The Hijra to Medina
beats.description: The Prophet and his followers left Mecca for a nearby oasis city, where the first Muslim community took shape.

beats.title: Anan Founds Karaite Judaism
beats.description: A Babylonian scholar rejected the oral law and urged Jews to base their faith on scripture alone.

beats.title: Cluny Abbey Is Founded
beats.description: A Burgundian duke endowed a monastery answerable only to the pope, which became the head of a vast reforming order.

beats.title: The Druze Faith Emerges
beats.description: Preachers in Cairo proclaimed a new doctrine around the Fatimid ruler, founding a secretive faith still practised in the Levant.
beats.note: Britannica: propagation began in Cairo in 1017; origin sometimes given as 1017-1018.

beats.title: Bruno Founds the Carthusians
beats.description: A German-born scholar and six companions built a hermitage in the Alps, starting an order of silent contemplatives.

beats.title: Cistercians Founded at Cîteaux
beats.description: Monks left a wealthy abbey to follow the Benedictine rule more strictly in a Burgundian marsh, founding a new order.

beats.title: The Knights Templar Are Founded
beats.description: A French knight and a few companions vowed to protect pilgrims in the Holy Land, forming a famed military order.

beats.title: Peter Waldo Starts the Waldensians
beats.description: A wealthy Lyon merchant gave up his goods to preach in poverty, inspiring a lay movement later condemned as heretical.

beats.title: Teutonic Knights Are Founded
beats.description: German crusaders besieging Acre set up a field hospital that grew into a military religious order.
beats.note: Hospital brotherhood 1190; papal recognition 1192, military order 1198.

beats.title: Francis Founds the Franciscans
beats.description: An Italian merchant's son who embraced poverty won verbal approval for a simple rule for his band of brothers.

beats.title: Dominic Founds the Dominicans
beats.description: A Castilian priest won approval for an order of preaching friars devoted to teaching and countering heresy.

beats.title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
beats.description: A German monk's challenge to the sale of indulgences set off the Reformation and the split of Western Christianity.

beats.title: The First Anabaptist Baptisms
beats.description: Radical reformers in Zurich rebaptised one another as adults, breaking with both Rome and the city's reformers.

beats.title: Henry VIII's Act of Supremacy
beats.description: Parliament declared the English king head of the church, ending the authority of Rome over it.
beats.why_in: founding of the Church of England

beats.title: Calvin Publishes the Institutes
beats.description: A young French theologian set out a systematic Protestant doctrine that became the basis of the Reformed churches.

beats.title: Ignatius Founds the Jesuits
beats.description: The pope approved a new order of priests led by a former Basque soldier, bound by a special vow of obedience to him.

beats.title: Scotland Founds a Presbyterian Kirk
beats.description: A Scottish parliament abolished papal authority and adopted a Reformed confession shaped by John Knox.
beats.why_in: founding of the Church of Scotland

beats.title: Teresa Founds Discalced Carmelites
beats.description: A Spanish nun opened a tiny, austere convent in Avila, beginning a reform of her order.

beats.title: Smyth Founds the First Baptists
beats.description: English exiles in Amsterdam baptised themselves as believers, forming the first congregation of its kind.

beats.title: George Fox Founds the Quakers
beats.description: After a vision on an English hilltop, a preacher gathered the Religious Society of Friends.

beats.title: Ammann Founds the Amish
beats.description: A Swiss Anabaptist elder broke from the Mennonites over strict shunning and plain living.

beats.title: Herrnhut Becomes a Moravian Home
beats.description: Persecuted Protestants settled on a German count's estate and renewed the Moravian Church there.

beats.title: Wesley's Heart Strangely Warmed
beats.description: At a London meeting an Anglican priest felt assurance of salvation, igniting the Methodist movement.

beats.title: Ann Lee Brings Shakers to America
beats.description: An English preacher led a small band across the Atlantic to found a celibate communal sect in New York.
beats.why_in: founding of the Shakers in America
beats.note: Arrival in New York; sect began in England earlier.

beats.title: Seesen Reform Temple Opens
beats.description: A German banker built a school-synagogue with an organ and German prayers, a seed of Reform Judaism.

beats.title: Smith Founds the Church of Christ
beats.description: A New York farmer who published a new scripture organised a church that became the Latter-day Saints.

beats.title: Seventh-day Adventists Organise
beats.description: Followers of a Sabbath-keeping, Second Coming movement formed a general conference in Michigan.

beats.title: Booth Founds the Salvation Army
beats.description: A Methodist preacher began a mission to the poor of London's East End that became a uniformed charity church.

beats.title: Eddy Charters Christian Science
beats.description: A New England author who taught that illness yields to prayer chartered her own church in Boston.

beats.title: Watch Tower Society Is Incorporated
beats.description: Followers of Charles Taze Russell formed a Pennsylvania company to publish literature, the root of Jehovah's Witnesses.

beats.title: Azusa Street Revival Begins
beats.description: Prayer meetings in a Los Angeles mission, marked by speaking in tongues, launched a global movement.

beats.title: Escriva Founds Opus Dei
beats.description: A young Spanish priest said he saw a vision of a lay-focused work, starting a Catholic institution.

beats.title: Rastafari Begins with a Coronation
beats.description: The crowning of an Ethiopian emperor was hailed by Jamaican preachers as the fulfilment of prophecy, launching a new faith.

beats.title: Roger Schutz Starts Taize
beats.description: A Swiss Protestant settled in a small French village to shelter refugees, beginning an ecumenical monastic community.

beats.title: Missionaries of Charity Founded
beats.description: A nun in Calcutta won approval for a new congregation to serve the poorest of the poor.
beats.note: Not re-verified by search; widely cited as 1950.

beats.title: Scientology Is Founded
beats.description: A science fiction author's self-help system Dianetics was reorganised as a religion with its first church incorporated.
beats.note: First church incorporated in New Jersey in December 1953; not re-verified by search.

beats.title: LaVey Founds the Church of Satan
beats.description: A San Francisco showman proclaimed a new year and an atheistic religion built on indulgence and individualism.
beats.note: Founded Walpurgisnacht 1966 per Wikipedia and Britannica.
